newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE KEEN TO MAINTAIN ONE-DAY SUPERIORITY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE KEEN TO MAINTAIN ONE-DAY SUPERIORITY.

text.p: Zimbabwean cricketers are not short of humility but there is an air of confidence before Sunday's opening one-day international against England.
Zimbabwe have only won seven of their 62 matches international limited overs games, but two of those wins have come against England.
The most famous was in Albury, Australia, during the 1992 World Cup when a chicken farmer by the name of Eddo Brandes took four for 21 and England went down by nine runs.
Brandes has been in and out of the side since then, but his presence in Sunday's team is one of the reasons the locals are anticipating another upset.
The other, and principal reason, is that, with few exceptions, England have been unimpressive on this tour so far. They lost twice to Mashonaland and struggled to overcome lowly Matabeleland.
The Queen's Club pitch is likely to be batsman friendly and with short boundaries the side batting first will need a large score to have a chance of winning.
Zimbabwe look set to pitch 37-year-old Andy Waller into the top of the order as a pinch hitter, while England's top six are unlikely to be tampered with.
The one question mark is over the fitness of all rounder Ronnie Irani, who left the field with a back strain against Matabeleland. But on current form Irani may lose his place to Andy Caddick anyway.
With left arm spinner Phil Tufnell not part of England's one-day plans, Yorkshire seamer Chris Silverwood is standing by to make his debut.
Zimbabwe: Alistair Campbell (captain), Grant Flower, Andy Waller, Guy Whittall, Dave Houghton, Andy Flower, Craig Evans, Heath Streak, Paul Strang, Eddo Brandes, John Rennie.
England (probable): Mike Atherton, Nick Knight, Alec Stewart, Nasser Hussain, Graham Thorpe, John Crawley, Robert Croft, Darren Gough, Andy Caddick, Allan Mullally, Chris Silverwood.
